description: A faint, straight east–west–trending ditch or canal segment approximately 160 m long, cutting across otherwise uniform low‐relief terrain. On the DTM hillshade it appears as a narrow linear depression with consistent width (~2–3 m), and in the Sentinel-2 NIR it corresponds to a band of elevated moisture/vegetation stress. No modern road or skid trail is mapped here in OpenStreetMap.

A second straight segment, trending northwest–southeast for roughly 200 m, visible as a shallow ridge-and-furrow pattern on the LiDAR DTM. It forms an unusually rectilinear alignment amidst natural hummocks. The feature also shows a subtle spectral signature in the visual band (slightly higher reflectance) and a contrasting tone in the NIR, indicative of differential soil moisture or anthropogenic soil fill.
